item.title: Impetigo Outbreak, Poverty Statistics, Budget Surplus
item.ns0:title: Impetigo Outbreak, Poverty Statistics, Budget Surplus
item.description:
Tonight on Our News, health officials report encouraging signs that the spread of impetigo appears to be slowing across New Providence and Grand Bahama, even as new cases continue to emerge. Meanwhile, health and safety concerns erupt at Freeport Primary School as union leaders demand swift action following reports of bats inside classrooms causing staff illness. Plus, newly released figures reveal up to 15 percent of Family Island residents are living below the poverty line, while a reported $39.3 million government budget surplus sparks fierce debate in Parliament alongside rising frustrations over gas prices nearing $8 a gallon. Tune in for all these top headlines, an investigation into inmate medical care, local sports highlights, and your complete weekend weather forecast!
